final_message:
DONE

I built the three-tab workbook, and all eight month-end balances agree to the GL. The one exception is a half-cent rounding difference on Prepaid Insurance in March. I recalculated the formulas outside Excel to check this (no spreadsheet application was available) and found no formula errors. The file has no stored values, so Excel will calculate it when you open it.

- **Prepaid Expenses (1250):** The 4/30 balance is **$559,377.61**, with YTD invoices of $1,087,156.21 and YTD amortization of $527,778.60. No invoice states an amortization period, so each is amortized over six months from its invoice month.
- **Prepaid Insurance (1251):** The 4/30 balance is **$369,976.70**, with YTD invoices of $568,698.22 and YTD amortization of $198,721.52. Good Insurance is spread over 12 months from January.
- **Totals:** Combined prepaids at 4/30 are $929,354.30 against a GL of $929,354.31. The extra cent is the rounding difference described below.

**BCBS timing:** I treated each monthly invoice as a prepayment of the *next* month's coverage, since coverage starts 2/1 and the first payment was due 1/15. So the January invoice is expensed in February, and a $5,493.27 prepaid balance sits at every month-end. This is the only treatment that ties to the GL. Under it, the April invoice is expensed in May.

**Rounding:** I did not round the monthly expense per invoice. March Prepaid Insurance computes to exactly $415,537.125 against a GL of $415,537.13, so the workbook treats gaps of half a cent or less as rounding. That is noted in the workbook.

**Expense accounts:** COA.xlsx lists expense accounts only, so I took 1250 and 1251 from your assignment and mapped each invoice type to an expense account.
- IT Services goes to 6760 and Subscription to 6762.
- Building Maintenance goes to 6020 and Technical Services Fee to 7001.
- Good Insurance goes to 5400 and BCBS to 5015.
- UHY "Advising" went to 5720 Consulting Fees, which is my judgment call. If UHY's work is accounting or audit, 5730 would be the better fit, so please confirm.

The `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders and the operations-records registry mentioned in the brief weren't in the folder, so I worked only from the PDFs and COA.xlsx. The workbook also lists "ADOBE MAGENTO" (January) and "Magento" (April) as separate vendors, as invoiced.

Each schedule tab has invoice-level amortization, month-end balances, a roll-forward against the GL, and an expense-by-account table for the journal entry.
